title: gen-8 deliberation hardening before the first real docket: speaker eligibility, vote-before-schedule, concluder attribution, case linkage
description: Close the gaps the gen-8 survey found in .harness/bin/deliberate.py so the first real docket runs under them: (1) cmd_schedule applies assembly_eligibility to every --speakers entry (clerk seats and unissued names refused, fail closed with the same 'roster inconsistent' posture as ballots) and records who scheduled (--by, eligibility-checked); (2) cmd_vote refuses when the dossier status is not 'deliberating' (a ballot before schedule is refused with a named reason, not silently accepted); (3) cmd_conclude takes --by (eligibility-checked, non-clerk) and records concluded_by; (4) propose accepts --case C-NNN and stores it as dossier.case; conclude refuses if dossier.case names a case that is not registered and open in precedent.py's register; (5) do NOT add a clerk gate to precedent.py publish (W-002 assigns fed-codificador the office of turning consensus into a record; that contradiction is for a docket or the operator, not for you) but ADD a read-only report verb or flag in precedent.py that prints, for a --case, whether the disposing record's published_by is a clerk seat, an issued non-clerk name, or unissued (report only, no refusal); (6) fix the one-sentence documentation discrepancy in CLAUDE.md: trust/ public material IS git-tracked (root.pub, root.fingerprint, constitutional payload+sig); private keys never are; keep the sentence that trust/ is writable by every agent. Do NOT edit .harness/operator-rulings-2026-08-22.md: it is signed and its bytes are covered by the signature. Update test_deliberate.py with a test per guard (each must fail against a guard-neutered copy). Full suite green. Standing rules: claim with blackboard.py claim <ID> --agent <you>; lock every file you edit with lock.py acquire; no emojis; nothing tracked may contain user paths, sibling-project names or personal tooling; never sign anything; never touch .harness/keys, trust/, constitutional/; never route around prevent_data_loss.py; commit is done by the coordinator, not you; hand off with blackboard.py handoff <ID> --agent <you> --to-role verifier with replayable evidence (exact commands + expected output). A crash is not a refusal: fail closed with a named reason.

EXPECTED vs ACTUAL: expected all 5 items (schedule speaker+scheduler eligibility, vote-before-schedule refusal, conclude --by eligibility, case linkage, precedent.py read-only publisher-report) to close the gen-8 survey gaps without breaking the existing D-001-regression suite. ACTUAL: implemented items 1-6; one pre-existing test (TheD001DefectCannotRecur::test_a_non_clerk_docket_still_cannot_skip_discussion) needed --by added to its schedule/conclude calls since the real roster.json fixture has no 'main' seat -- fixed, not worked around. Full suite: 897 passed, 4 skipped (pre-existing skips, unrelated). Mutation-check performed on scratch copies under <session-scratchpad>/mutants (never on the live files): each of the 4 deliberate.py guards and the precedent.py classify_seat/CLERK_MARKERS-drift guard were individually neutered and the corresponding new tests were confirmed to FAIL against the neutered copy and PASS against the pristine copy.

HANDOFF -> verifier: Built all 6 items of T-428's spec. Files touched: .harness/bin/deliberate.py, .harness/bin/precedent.py, .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py, .harness/tests/test_precedent_case_publisher_report.py (new), claude.md.

ITEM 1 (schedule eligibility): cmd_schedule now takes --by (scheduler, eligibility-checked via assembly_eligibility before the guarded block) and runs assembly_eligibility over every entry of the EFFECTIVE speaker list (explicit --speakers or the sponsors+priors default), refusing the WHOLE call on the first ineligible entry with the same clerk-seat/unissued-name/roster-inconsistent posture as a ballot. Records dossier.scheduled_by.
Replay: python3 .harness/bin/lock.py acquire (n/a, read-only replay) then:
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py::ScheduleEligibilityGuards -v
Expected: 6 passed (4 refusal cases: clerk speaker, unissued speaker, clerk scheduler, unissued scheduler; 2 negative controls: eligible schedule succeeds and records scheduled_by; rosterless bootstrap unaffected).

ITEM 2 (vote-before-schedule refusal): cmd_vote now refuses unless dossier status == 'deliberating' exactly (previously also accepted 'sponsored', which is D-001's actual defect: a ballot with no speaker order and no chance to discuss). Named refusal message points at `schedule`.
Replay: python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py::VoteBeforeScheduleIsRefused -v
Expected: 3 passed.

ITEM 3 (conclude --by): cmd_conclude takes --by (eligibility-checked, non-clerk, same assembly_eligibility gate), refused before the dossier is even loaded on an ineligible name; records dossier.concluded_by.
Replay: python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py::ConcludeEligibilityGuards -v
Expected: 3 passed.

ITEM 4 (case linkage): `propose --case C-NNN` stores dossier.case (format-checked only at write time); `conclude` re-validates it against precedent.py's LIVE case register (precedent.cases_dir/load_case, imported as a module -- deliberate.py -> precedent.py is one-directional, no cycle) -- unregistered or no-longer-open both refuse, never trusted from propose time.
Replay: python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py::CaseLinkageGuard -v
Expected: 6 passed.

ITEM 5 (precedent.py read-only report, explicitly NOT a publish gate): new `precedent.py case publisher-report C-NNN [--json]` verb + `classify_seat(hroot, name)` helper classify the name that published the record disposing a case as clerk/issued-non-clerk/unissued/no-roster/roster-inconsistent. `publish` itself carries zero new checks -- proven by a negative-control test that a clerk-seated --agent still publishes successfully and the report then classifies it 'clerk'. CLERK_MARKERS is duplicated (not imported, to avoid a circular import since deliberate.py already imports precedent.py) and pinned equal to deliberate.py's constant by a dedicated cross-module test.
Replay: python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_precedent_case_publisher_report.py -v
Expected: 17 passed.

ITEM 6 (claude.md correction): fixed the false claim that .harness/trust/ is "untracked by git" -- `git ls-files .harness/trust` shows root.pub, root.fingerprint and README.md ARE tracked (and .harness/constitutional/reputation.json{,.sig} too), private keys never are. Kept the "trust/ is writable by every agent" sentence and its underlying point (git-tracked != protected against a same-session working-tree overwrite before the next commit). Did NOT touch .harness/operator-rulings-2026-08-22.md. NOTE for the verifier: .harness/tests/test_warrant.py:781-782 carries the same stale phrase in a docstring (not an assertion) -- left untouched as out of this task's declared scope (CLAUDE.md only); flagging for a follow-up task if wanted.
